title: Adaptive proration and automated rollback playbook for mid-cycle contract adjustments
creator: Mariko Tanaka
description:
Background: Enterprise customers frequently request mid-cycle contract changes (seat count, reserved capacity, or negotiated rate tiers) during procurement or after security questionnaire holds are cleared. Current billing logic applies a single pro-rata rule that often leads to over-crediting or manual adjustments when committed capacity and metered usage cross thresholds in the same billing period. That creates operational toil for Billing Ops and bad experience for customers (delayed invoices, follow-up credits, and disputes).

Goal: Design and implement an 'Adaptive Proration & Automated Rollback' playbook that:
- Automatically calculates fair, auditable credits and debits for mid-cycle contract changes across token-based metering and reserved capacity tiers.
- Supports contractual overrides for negotiated enterprise deals while minimizing manual intervention.
- Implements a billing-quarantine / provisional-invoice stage for accounts under Security Questionnaire or contractual review, with automated rollback or finalization flows when the hold is resolved.

Scope (in):
- Token and embedding metering adjustments when customer changes plan mid-cycle.
- Reserved capacity adjustments (partial month purchase/sale, burst allowances) with time-weighted credit computation.
- Provisional invoice generation and a 'quarantine window' for accounts with active legal/SQ holds.
- Automated rollback mechanism to revert provisional charges if a dispute or security hold triggers reversal conditions within the configured window.

Scope (out):
- Full ledger re-architect (we will extend existing ledger model instead). 
- International tax/proration rules (handled separately by Finance). 

Proposed approach (summary):
1) Canonical event model: treat every contract change as an immutable 'billing event' with timestamp, reason (upgrade/downgrade/negotiation/hold-clear), actor, and optional negotiation ID. Persist to billing-events table.
2) Time-weighted proration: compute credits using a normalized daily weighting across the billing cycle for token units and reserved capacity slots. For thresholds that change (e.g., moving between tiered discounts), compute delta using a two-segment integration (pre-change and post-change effective rates).
3) Safety-net provisional credits: when a Security Questionnaire or contract dispute is open, generate a provisional invoice and provisional credits (visible in Console as 'Pending adjustments') but do not post to the live ledger until the quarantine window closes or is resolved. Default quarantine window = 14 days (configurable per enterprise).
4) Automated rollback: define deterministic rollback triggers (hold re-opened, dispute marked customer-favorable, negative-balance safety threshold) that schedule a reversal job. Reversals create a explicit reversal event and ledger entry; they also open an operational ticket if reversal amount > $X (configurable). 
5) Audit trail + customer notices: every auto-credit/debit must include a reason code and link to the originating billing-event and contract version. Console will show 'Why this credit' flows and downloadable CSV for Finance reconciliation.

Trade-offs considered:
- Simpler pro-rata (single-day rule) is easier but leads to edge-case disputes with negotiated tier boundaries; the time-weighted approach is more complex but significantly reduces manual refunds. 
- Holding provisional charges delays revenue recognition for a small cohort; Finance OK'ed provisional staging for security-hold high-risk customers only.
- Rolling back programmatically requires robust testing of dependent downstream systems (reporting, BI, refunds). We prefer explicit reversal events vs. in-place mutation to keep auditability.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Billing engine can compute and apply credits for >=95% of mid-cycle events without human intervention in staging test scenarios.
- Console shows pending adjustments and links to billing-event, and Finance can export reconciliation CSV that matches ledger.
- Automated rollback path executes and produces a reversal entry and customer notification within configured SLO (default: 24 hours after trigger).

Additional notes: we must coordinate with Legal for contract versioning metadata and with Finance for revenue recognition guidance.
decision_log: 2026-03-11: PM review - adopt time-weighted proration instead of best-effort single-day rule (PM, Finance agree).
2026-03-12: Engineering feasibility sync - event model acceptable, but ENG requests bounded job window to avoid heavy compute at month-end.
2026-03-13: Security flagged quarantine flows; security review required before enabling prototype for accounts with PII-heavy customers.
updates: 2026-03-10 - Initial ticket created by Mariko with example customer scenarios (ACME mid-cycle downgrade, Zenith negotiated bursting credit, SecureBank security questionnaire clearance).
2026-03-11 - Finance provided sample ledger rows and suggested default quarantine window = 14 days. Attached sample CSV in links.
2026-03-12 - Eng spike scheduled; ENG-4123 allocated 3 days to prototype event model and proration calculator. Diego assigned for coordination.
2026-03-12 - PM posted mockups of Console 'Pending adjustments' panel in drive (link below). UX suggests explicit 'Accept' button for manual override by Finance users.

acceptance_criteria: Automated compute: for 10 synthetic enterprise scenarios (documented), the system computes identical credits to Finance's spreadsheet within 0.5% tolerance.
Provisional invoices are visible in Console with explanatory text and a link to billing-event IDs.
Rollback path produces a reversal ledger entry, a notification to Billing Ops, and a customer-facing email template is sent within 24 hours of trigger.
Auditability: every adjustment row contains origin_event_id and contract_version; exported CSV contains these columns and matches totals to the ledger.
Performance: background reconciliation jobs complete under 2 hours for the largest enterprise account tested (>= 10M tokens/day).
notes: Implementation considerations: ensure idempotency for billing-event processing, add feature flag to gate provisional-invoice functionality, expose admin override in Console guarded by RBAC. Risk: month-end compute spikes; recommend staged rollout and sampling. Operational playbook draft to be added to Confluence with step-by-step for manual reversal cases and contact list for Finance + Legal.
implementation_strategy: Phase 1 (spike): build billing-event model, unit-test time-weighted calculator, run against Finance CSV samples (ENG-4123).
Phase 2 (pilot): enable provisional invoices for 5 enterprise accounts with Finance oversight; collect reconciliation feedback (2 billing cycles).
Phase 3 (rollout): expand to all accounts with security-hold flag and enable default 14-day quarantine; monitor metrics and iterate on SLOs.
